newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore saddened by row with Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore saddened by row with Malaysia.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Saturday he was saddened by a row that has disrupted relations with Malaysia and vowed to improve ties with Kuala Lumpur.
Goh said in a statement he welcomed an assurance by Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad that media reports of a freeze in relations with the city state were inaccurate.
The row first erupted after Singapore elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew described the southern Malaysian state of Johor as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
"I am saddened that our bilateral relations have been upset by (the) Senior Minister's remarks on Johor," Goh said.
Malaysians reacted with fury. Members of the youth wing of the ruling UMNO party of Mahathir called Lee "senile" and Malaysia's foreign minister called for an apology and a retraction.

"Senior Minister (Lee) had said that it was never his intention to cause offence. In fact, Senior Minister had immediately apologised to me when the remarks became public. He has also apologised to the Malaysians," Goh said.

"We believe that closer cooperation between Malaysia and Singapore will benefit both countries. We will do our part to restore and improve cooperation at a pace Malaysia is comfortable with," he added.
The statement came one day after Malaysia said it wanted to end the acrimonious dispute while asking that Singapore's leaders show some "earnestness" in its dealings with Kuala Lumpur.

"We therefore regret that some members of the Singapore government seem to lack insight and earnestness, even appear to trivialise what is at issue," a statement by Malaysia Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday.
Lee had apologised and instructed his lawyer to ask the Singapore court to strike out his remarks from the affidavit, filed in relation to a libel suit against opposition politician Tang Liang Hong.
Tang, who lost a hotly contested race in the January 2 elections in Singapore, fled to Johor after claiming he had received death threats.
Tang urged Lee to resign because of the row's damaging effect on relations between the two neighbours.

"It is time for Lee to leave the cabinet so that he can no longer embarrass the Singapore people as well as damage the existing good relations between the two countries," Tang told reporters in a briefing on Friday in Johor.
Tang also called on Goh to have his government take responsibility for Lee's actions.
"As a political leader, you can't say that it has nothing to do with the cabinet, especially if he (Lee) is the next most important member (of the government) after himself," Tang said.
"As a Singaporean, I say it is shameful that our country is running along in such a limping duck fashion."
The Malaysian railway company KTM Berhad said on Saturday it had issued 168 eviction notices against people occupying its land in Singapore.

The operation to issue the notices, which began on Thursday and ended on Saturday, was launched against private operators who used KTM's land as dumping grounds, storage yards, make-shift housing for foreign workers and as scrap metal yards.
The squatters were given seven days to leave the properties or face charges for damages, trespass and legal costs, the KTM statement said.
KTM owns more than 200 hectares (500 acres) of land in Singapore on a 999-year lease dating back to the time when both were still British colonies
